newsitem.title: ITALY: BankNapoli stock surges in Milan.
newsitem.headline: BankNapoli stock surges in Milan.

text.p: Banco di Napoli savings shares rose sharply in strong volume on the Milan stock exchange as interest in the troubled southern bank continued after this week's official approval of a rescue plan.

The struggling Naples bank is due for privastisation later this year as part of the bail-out package. Potential buyers have until November 18 to declare their interest in the sale of an initial 60 percent of the heavily indebted bank.
"As we're getting near to the moment the bank will be taken over and brought back to health, people are starting to buy up the stock," one dealer said.
At 1320 GMT, Banco di Napoli savings shares, the only one quoted, were up 9.40 percent at 610 lire with over 330,000 shares changing hands against an average 230,000 over the last month.
Banco di Napoli senior managers were quoted in Friday's financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore as saying the bank could break even in 1997 and return to profit in 1998.
The bank had record losses of 3.12 trillion lire in 1995 and plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year.
